title: Information and Burden in Micro-Randomized Trials with Cooldowns and Daily Prompt Caps
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded the fully proved immediate-outcome benchmark incremental below the field floor; a source-faithful SeqRTS comparison eliminates the only certified gap.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the normalized homogeneous conditional immediate-effect information–burden and cap frontiers, fixed-cap saturation, parity behavior, and a restricted D=3 SeqRTS separation; the math panel passed. The field-tier extension failed its early kill: source-faithful SeqRTS with three singleton blocks exactly matched the oracle at J₃=9425/16384 and burden 2123/2048, while the remaining finite-day optimum is a routine Bellman recursion. The two-hour marginal Sense2Stop target requires additional identification and covariance structure and remains outside this model.
tldr: What is the sharp information–burden frontier for a common conditional immediate causal effect when prompting removes future randomization opportunities and a hard daily cap stops delivery? Under exogenous iid permission and eligible-state positivity, the paper establishes a global three-regime frontier over history-dependent policies, with a causal potential-outcome identification and oracle-score contract. It also proves finite-day structure and a restricted SeqRTS comparison, while leaving the actual two-hour marginal Sense2Stop target to a separately scoped extension.
gap: Sense2Stop has a post-prompt exclusion and a six-prompt daily cap, so each assignment changes future randomization opportunities. The inspected MRT and adjacent renewal, dead-time, and operational-capacity results do not state the sharp sequencewise information–burden and within-person cap frontier for a common conditional immediate effect under the present floor and iid-permission model. This is a bounded source audit, not proof that no unlocated work exists.
fill: Establish the global burden and cap frontiers after identifying the common conditional causal effect, quantify the cooldown penalty and finite-horizon structure, and delineate the separate precision problem for marginal overlapping outcomes.
